verses.text: God remembered Noah, all the animals, and all the livestock that were with him in the ship; and God made a wind to pass over the earth. The waters subsided.
The deep’s fountains and the sky’s windows were also stopped, and the rain from the sky was restrained.
The waters continually receded from the earth. After the end of one hundred fifty days the waters decreased.
The ship rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on Ararat’s mountains.
The waters receded continually until the tenth month. In the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains were visible.
At the end of forty days, Noah opened the window of the ship which he had made,
and he sent out a raven. It went back and forth, until the waters were dried up from the earth.
He himself sent out a dove to see if the waters were abated from the surface of the ground,

but the dove found no place to rest her foot, and she returned into the ship to him, for the waters were on the surface of the whole earth. He put out his hand, and took her, and brought her to him into the ship.
He waited yet another seven days; and again he sent the dove out of the ship.
The dove came back to him at evening and, behold, in her mouth was a freshly plucked olive leaf. So Noah knew that the waters were abated from the earth.
He waited yet another seven days, and sent out the dove; and she didn’t return to him anymore.

In the six hundred first year, in the first month, the first day of the month, the waters were dried up from the earth. Noah removed the covering of the ship, and looked. He saw that the surface of the ground was dried.
In the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth was dry.
God spoke to Noah, saying,
“Go out of the ship, you, your wife, your sons, and your sons’ wives with you.

Bring out with you every living thing that is with you of all flesh, including birds, livestock, and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth, that they may breed abundantly in the earth, and be fruitful, and multiply on the earth.”
Noah went out, with his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives with him.
Every animal, every creeping thing, and every bird, whatever moves on the earth, after their families, went out of the ship.
Noah built an altar to Yahweh, and took of every clean animal, and of every clean bird, and offered burnt offerings on the altar.

Yahweh smelled the pleasant aroma. Yahweh said in his heart, “I will not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake because the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth. I will never again strike every living thing, as I have done.
While the earth remains, seed time and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night will not cease.”

footnotes.content: I take comfort that the first thing Scripture says after the flood is that God remembered Noah. He hadn't forgotten him in that long year of waiting. And the wind He sent shows that the One who judged also gently stirs the waters to begin the work of restoration.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The fountains of the deep and the windows of heaven that once burst open are now closed by the same hand. Our God both opens and shuts, and when He shuts the floodgates, it's because mercy has a purpose.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: One hundred fifty days of receding waters remind me that God's restoration often moves slowly. I want instant change, but our faithful God patiently brings dry ground in His own time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After months of tossing, the ship finally found rest on the mountains of Ararat. I think of how those in Christ, after long storms, will at last find true and lasting rest in the One who has brought us through.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Day by day the peaks began to show again, like hope returning little by little. The God who hides the mountains in judgment will, in mercy, bring them back into view for those He is saving.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Forty more days and Noah opened the window he had made. After waiting on God's timing all this time, I notice his faithful patience. Sometimes the godly must watch and wait even after they see hope on the horizon.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The raven went to and fro until the waters dried up. It's a plain bird doing a plain task, but I see a picture of restless searching over a ruined world. How different from the dove that would seek rest in Christ alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Noah sends forth the dove, a gentle creature longing for a place to rest. My heart is much like that dove before I knew the Lord - restless until I found rest in Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The dove found no place to rest her foot, so she returned to Noah. How like us - the world that has been judged has no safe resting place for the redeemed. We must return to the refuge God has provided in the ark.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Again Noah waited seven days. I wish I had more of that quiet faithfulness - willing to wait on the Lord rather than rushing out of His appointed time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The dove returned with a freshly plucked olive leaf - a small gift of hope from a renewed earth. For centuries, the olive tree has spoken of peace, and I can't help but look beyond it to the Prince of Peace who would one day bring true reconciliation between God and man.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After one last seven-day wait, the dove didn't return. The time of abiding in the ark was over; it was time to go forth. The Lord knows exactly when the season of refuge gives way to the season of walking in the new world.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: On that first day of the first month, Noah uncovered the ark and saw dry ground. I wonder what joy filled his aged heart after so long. How much greater will be the joy when we see the new heavens and new earth, freed at last from all judgment!
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God's word of restoration was complete to the day. The earth was fully dry as He had ordained. Our Lord never leaves His work half done - what He has promised to restore, He will surely bring to completion.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After all that time, the command still comes: 'God spoke to Noah.' The One who shut them in is the same One who now calls them out. His timing is perfect, and His word is faithful.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Noah, his family, and all with him are called forth as a new beginning. I think of God's people - brought through judgment safely only by grace, and now commissioned to go forth under His blessing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The command to be fruitful and multiply echoes the blessing given at creation. Though sin remains, God's original purpose for life to fill the earth is not abandoned. In Christ, He will one day fully restore all things to what He intended.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Noah went out in faith, obeying the word of the Lord. After such a long stay, I can imagine both relief and wonder. Faith trusts God to call us out when He says the time has come.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every kind went out after their families, just as God had ordained. The same God who preserved each kind in the ark will preserve all that belongs to Him through every storm until He brings them safely home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The first thing Noah does on dry ground is build an altar to Yahweh. A man saved by grace worships first. Before building a home or planting crops, he gives the best of what God has preserved back to the God who preserved it all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh smelled the pleasing aroma of that sacrifice. I long to know that my worship through Christ is also pleasing to Him, for our sacrifices can never satisfy - only the perfect sacrifice of Jesus truly delights the Father's heart and turns away judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo of God's faithfulness in the changing of the seasons. As of 2026-10, I find myself grateful that the same God who established seedtime and harvest still upholds all things, and will one day make all things new.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
